CheckTitle: Repository has secret scanning push protection enabled to block commits containing secrets
Description: **GitHub repository** configuration for **secret scanning push protection**-which rejects pushes containing supported secret patterns (API keys, tokens, private keys) before they reach the Git history-is evaluated to determine if the block is active.
Risk: Without **push protection**, secret scanning only alerts after a credential is already in the Git history and visible to anyone with read access, forks or clones. During that exposure window attackers can gain **unauthorized access** to cloud and third-party services or compromise the **supply chain** through leaked deployment tokens, degrading **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

Code.CLI: gh api -X PATCH repos/<OWNER>/<REPO> -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"security_and_analysis":{"secret_scanning":{"status":"enabled"},"secret_scanning_push_protection":{"status":"enabled"}}}'
Code.Other:
1. In GitHub, open the target repository and go to Settings
2. In the left sidebar, click Code security and analysis
3. Under Secret scanning, make sure Secret scanning is Enabled
4. Under Push protection, click Enable
5. Confirm if prompted

Recommendation.Text:
Enable **secret scanning push protection** on every repository, or enable it organization-wide so new repositories inherit it.
- Keep **secret scanning** enabled; push protection depends on it
- Enable **delegated bypass** so exceptions are reviewed instead of silently allowed
- Store secrets in a dedicated **secrets manager**, never in code
- Rotate any credential that was pushed before protection was active

Notes: Push protection requires secret scanning to be enabled on the repository. Repositories whose security settings could not be read are not reported.
